---
title: "Response timeline"
---

When responses came in, by day. Two requests were sent to conference
participants:

- **2023-07-08** — 1st circular
- **2023-07-17** — 2nd circular (reminder)

```{python}
# | echo: false
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import altair as alt
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd().parent))
from _helpers import load_public  # noqa: E402

df = load_public()
daily = (
    pd.to_datetime(df["timestamp"])
    .dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    .value_counts()
    .rename_axis("date")
    .reset_index(name="responses")
    .sort_values("date")
)
requests = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "date": ["2023-07-08", "2023-07-17"],
        "label": ["1st circular", "2nd circular"],
    }
)
```

```{python}
# | echo: false
bars = (
    alt.Chart(daily)
    .mark_bar()
    .encode(
        x=alt.X("date:T", title=None),
        y=alt.Y("responses:Q", title="Responses"),
        tooltip=["date:T", "responses:Q"],
    )
)
rules = (
    alt.Chart(requests)
    .mark_rule(color="firebrick", strokeDash=[4, 4])
    .encode(x="date:T", tooltip=["label:N"])
)
(bars + rules).properties(width="container", height=300, title="Responses per day")
```

Most responses arrived within three days of the first circular, with a
smaller bump after the reminder.

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Counts are from the anonymized extract (245 of 295 respondents; the
rest were removed by k-anonymity). Timestamps are truncated to the day.
:::
